extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when applicant actions or inactions trigger reductions in patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704 (including calculation windows, caps, exceptions, and safe-harbors).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) — Failure to timely withdraw holding of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not request withdrawal of the holding of abandonment within two months of the mailing of a notice of abandonment, the applicant has failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution and any patent term adjustment will be reduced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment set forth in 37 CFR 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date two months from the date of mailing of the notice of abandonment and ending on the date a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive the application was filed. If a petition is granted, OPSG system records should be checked and corrected if necessary; applicants are encouraged to check OPSG records via the USPTO electronic filing system and contact the examiner, supervisor, or Technology Center service representative if papers or dates are recorded incorrectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(5) — Conversion of a provisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination (37 CFR 1.704(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) and ending on the date a request in compliance with 37 CFR 1.53(c)(3) to convert the provisional application into a nonprovisional application was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(6) — Submission of a preliminary amendment or paper (timing close to Office action/allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before the mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires the mailing of a supplemental Office action or notice of allowance is a circumstance constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(c)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission requires issuance of a supplemental Office action/notice of allowance, it has interfered with processing. For notices of allowance mailed on or after July 16, 2020, reduction is the number of days beginning on the day after the date that is eight months from filing (or national stage commencement) and ending on the date the preliminary amendment was filed. For other applications, the period reduced is the lesser of (a) days beginning the day after the mailing date of the original Office action/notice of allowance and ending on the mailing date of the supplemental Office action/notice of allowance, or (b) four months (four-month cap).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(7) — Submission of a reply with an omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a reply having an omission (e.g., requiring an action under 37 CFR 1.135(c)) is a circumstance constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination (37 CFR 1.704(c)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date the reply having an omission was filed and ending on the date the reply or other paper correcting the omission was filed. The provision is not limited to 1.135(c) and applies to any Office action/notice indicating a reply omission (e.g., petitions dismissed under 1.47 or non-compliant sequence listings). Filing of a non-compliant appeal brief will not be deemed an omission under 1.704(c)(7) if the notice of appeal was filed on or after September 17, 2012 (that situation is covered under 1.704(c)(11)). If applicant believes a PTA was reduced for a period with no identifiable effort by the applicant, a timely request for reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.705(b) may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8) — Submission of a supplemental reply or paper after a reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper (e.g., an IDS or petition) after an initial reply has been filed constitutes failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination (37 CFR 1.704(c)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date the initial reply was filed and ending on the date the supplemental reply or other paper was filed. An IDS filed after a reply to a restriction requirement (without the 1.704(d) safe harbor) or an IDS filed after an RCE but before a subsequent Office action is applicant delay. 1.704(c)(8) does not apply to supplemental papers expressly requested by the examiner. The Office will not reduce PTA in rare situations where there is 'no identifiable effort in which the applicant could have engaged' (see Supernus Pharm., Inc. v. Iancu). If an amendment is requested by the examiner, the examiner should process it so it is not flagged separately in OPSG.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(9) — Submission of an amendment or paper after Board or court decision (timing near OA/NOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or other paper (other than 41.50(c) statements) in an application after a decision by the PTAB or a federal court less than one month before the mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires mailing of a supplemental Office action/notice of allowance constitutes failure (37 CFR 1.704(c)(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For notices of allowance mailed on or after July 16, 2020, reduction is the number of days beginning on the day after the date of the Board or court decision and ending on the date the amendment or paper was filed. For other applications, reduction is the lesser of days beginning the day after the mailing date of the original Office action/notice of allowance and ending on the mailing date of the supplemental Office action/notice of allowance, or four months (four-month cap). Examiner-requested amendments should be processed to avoid separate OPSG flagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10) — Submission of an amendment or paper after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 or other paper (other than a request for continued examination in compliance with § 1.114) after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed is a circumstance constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination of an application (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 10, 2015, the rule was amended to exclude RCEs (treated under 1.704(c)(12)). For notices of allowance mailed on or after July 16, 2020, reduction is the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the amendment or other paper was filed, except for an amendment 'expressly requested by the Office.' For all other applications, reduction is the lesser of (1) the number of days beginning on the date the amendment/other paper was filed and ending on the mailing date of the Office action/notice in response to that paper, or (2) four months. The phrase 'expressly requested by the Office' requires a specific request in an Office action/notice or in an Examiner's Interview Summary (PTOL–413/413B); generic language is not sufficient. IDS in compliance with 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered a failure under 1.704(c)(10) (or c(6), c(8), c(9)) if accompanied by a statement under 1.704(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers not considered failures after a Notice of Allowance (exceptions under 1.704(c)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain papers filed after a Notice of Allowance are not considered failures to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing/examination and therefore do not trigger 1.704(c)(10) reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following are explicitly listed as not triggering a failure under 1.704(c)(10): (1) Fee(s) Transmittal (PTOL-85B); (2) power of attorney; (3) power to inspect; (4) change of address; (5) change of status (micro/small/not small entity status); (6) a response to the examiner's reasons for allowance or a request to correct an error or omission in the Notice of Allowance or Notice of Allowability; (7) status letters; (8) requests for a refund; (9) an inventor's oath or declaration; (10) an IDS with a statement in compliance with 1.704(d); (11) resubmission of unlocatable papers previously filed (37 CFR 1.251); (12) a request for acknowledgement of an IDS in compliance with 1.97/1.98 if the applicant had requested acknowledgement prior to the notice of allowance or it was applicant's first opportunity to request acknowledgement; (13) comments on the substance of an applicant-initiated interview that resulted in a notice of allowance; and (14) letters related to government interests (e.g., between NASA and the Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers that will be considered failures after a Notice of Allowance (per 1.704(c)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain papers filed after a Notice of Allowance are explicitly listed as causing PTA reductions under 1.704(c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 1.704(c)(10), the following will be considered failures: (1) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312; (2) a paper containing a claim for priority or benefit or request to correct priority/benefit information (e.g., new/supplemental application data sheet to correct foreign priority/domestic benefit); (3) a request for a corrected filing receipt; (4) a certified copy of a priority document; (5) drawings; (6) a letter related to biologic deposits; (7) a request to change or correct inventorship; and (8) an IDS not accompanied by a statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.704(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11) — Failure to timely file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications where a notice of appeal was filed on or after September 17, 2012, failure to file an appeal brief compliant with 37 CFR 41.37 within three months from the filing of the notice of appeal to the PTAB is a circumstance constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(c)(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 37 CFR 41.37 sets a two‑month deadline for filing an appeal brief, 1.704(c)(11) provides three months before any PTA under 1.703 will be reduced for late submission. If a non‑compliant appeal brief is followed by a compliant brief, the time from the non‑compliant to the compliant brief will not be considered a failure under 1.704(c)(8). If the compliant appeal brief is filed more than three months after the notice of appeal, 1.704(c)(11) may result in a PTA reduction. The period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by days beginning the day after three months from the date the notice of appeal was filed and ending on the date a compliant appeal brief or a request for continued examination under 1.114 was filed. If the Office reopens prosecution more than three months after filing the notice of appeal but before a compliant brief is filed, the period between the three‑month mark and the Office's reopening is not treated as applicant delay under 1.704(c)(11).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(12) — Filing of a request for continued examination (RCE) after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for RCEs filed on or after March 10, 2015, submission of a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after a notice of allowance has been mailed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination (37 CFR 1.704(c)(12)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed. This prevents applicants from obtaining additional PTA by delaying issuance through filing an RCE after allowance. An RCE in compliance with 1.114 that contains no submission other than an IDS in compliance with 1.97/1.98 will not be considered a failure if accompanied by a statement in compliance with 1.704(d). If an RCE is filed after payment of the issue fee, any PTA will be reduced by the days from the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance until the date the RCE was filed. Guidance is provided on how to determine the relevant issue‑fee date and how the Office treats reopening of prosecution and issue fee transmittal forms (PTOL‑85(b)). Note: 37 CFR 1.114 does not permit filing an RCE after the issue fee is paid as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(13) — Failure to timely provide an application in condition for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after December 18, 2013, and international applications with national stage commenced under 35 U.S.C. 371 on or after that date, failure to provide an application in condition for examination within eight months from filing or national stage commencement is a circumstance constituting failure (37 CFR 1.704(c)(13)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is eight months from filing (or national stage commencement) and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination. The rule does not require applications to be in condition for examination on filing to avoid reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(14) — Prosecution via a continuing application (effects on PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Further prosecution via a continuing application (continuation, divisional, continuation‑in‑part) is a circumstance constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination insofar as patent term adjustment shall not include any period prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent (37 CFR 1.704(c)(14)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing applications used to obtain further/new examination are not entitled to carry over PTA periods that occurred prior to the continuing application's actual filing date. Thus, delays in prior (or other) applications are not relevant to whether the application that resulted in the patent is entitled to PTA. Special CPA rules are described (e.g., CPA filing date and entitlement periods); delays before the filing date of an application are not relevant to whether an application is entitled to PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(d) — Information disclosure statement (IDS) safe harbor and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered (result in a reduction) under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(6), (c)(8), (c)(9), or (c)(10) if it is accompanied by a statement meeting the requirements of 37 CFR 1.704(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1.704(d) specifies the content/conditions for the statement (e.g., that each item of information was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office or other patent office communication) and other formal requirements; when the IDS meets 1.97/1.98 and is accompanied by a 1.704(d) statement (and payment where required), it is generally treated as not causing applicant delay. The manual also explains related relaxations (e.g., permitting submission to the Office of information cited in a patent office communication to a counterpart application without reduction if submitted within thirty days of receipt by a designated individual) and procedural details for acknowledgement under 1.97(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.705(b) when PTA reduced improperly
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant believes the Office has reduced the patent term adjustment for a period during which there was no identifiable effort the applicant could have engaged in to conclude prosecution, the applicant may file a timely request for reconsideration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.705(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remedy applies where the applicant can show that the reduction was improper (e.g., no actionable step the applicant could have taken), and the request should be filed in the manner/timing required by 1.705(b). The manual cites this remedy in the context of several applicant‑delay provisions and rare situations where the Office's reduction may be inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSG records accuracy and applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to check the Office’s OPSG (One Patent Service Gateway) system records for their applications to ensure correct term adjustment determinations and recorded dates/papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If receipts or replies (e.g., a March 2 reply) were not matched with the file and a petition to withdraw abandonment is granted, applicants should ensure the receipt is recorded in OPSG; if papers/dates are recorded incorrectly, applicants should contact the examiner, examiner’s supervisor, or Technology Center service representative to correct the entry. Examiner processing practices (e.g., including examiner-requested amendments as part of interview summaries or examiner's amendments rather than standalone papers) are intended to avoid OPSG flags that would reduce PTA.
